headline: Four acts ended waits of seven years or more for a Hot 20 #1 in 2026. Kacey Musgraves waited ten
dek: This has been the year of the comeback at the top. We looked at the longest gaps between #1s in Hot 20 history, and how many of them closed this year.
body: Fourteen songs have reached #1 on the Hot 20 so far in 2026, and four of them came from acts who hadn't been there in at least seven years. [[Cam]], [[Danielle Bradbery]], [[Kacey Musgraves]] and, two weeks ago, [[Kenny Chesney]] all ended some of the longest droughts in the chart's history. Four of the ten longest gaps between #1s ever recorded on the Hot 20 closed this year.

The record. The longest wait belongs to [[Luke Bryan]]. ‘Drink A Beer’ spent a week at #1 in February 2014, and his next #1, ‘Closing Time in California,’ didn't come until June 2025, 11 years and three months later. Second on the list is Musgraves, and third is the Dixie Chicks, who went from ‘Not Ready To Make Nice’ in August 2010 to ‘Gaslighter’ in July 2020, just short of ten years.

Ten years for Kacey. Musgraves was one of the Hot 20's steadiest acts early on. ‘Merry Go 'Round,’ ‘Keep It To Yourself,’ ‘Dime Store Cowgirl’ and ‘Fine’ all reached #1 between 2013 and 2016. Then nothing reached the top for a decade. ‘Fine’ spent its last week at #1 on April 21, 2016, and ‘Dry Spell’ arrived there on May 7, 2026, ten years and two weeks later. The title wrote the headline for us. She didn't wait long for the next one: ‘Loneliest Girl’ went to #1 in September and stayed four weeks, giving her six #1s in all.

Cam opened the year. The first #1 of 2026 was Cam's ‘Everblue,’ on the January 1 chart. It was her first time at the top since ‘Diane’ held #1 for four weeks in January 2018, a gap of nearly eight years. Her first #1, ‘Mayday,’ spent six weeks there in 2016. ‘Everblue’ held for one week, but it put her back on the list.

Danielle Bradbery's biggest hit came second. Bradbery's first #1, ‘Potential,’ lasted one week in October 2018. Her second, ‘Dent,’ reached #1 in February, seven years and four months later, and stayed five weeks. Most acts who come back after a long gap get a short visit. Bradbery came back with the longest run at #1 of her career.

Kenny Chesney makes 13. Last month we noted that Chesney was back in the top two for the first time since 2019. Two weeks ago ‘Silver Sands Marina’ finished the climb, and it has now held #1 for two weeks. His last #1 had been ‘Tip of My Tongue’ in November 2019, almost exactly seven years earlier. It's his 13th #1, the third-most in Hot 20 history behind [[Carrie Underwood]]'s 21 and [[Carly Pearce]]'s 18. Chesney was a #1 act in the chart's very first year, with ‘The Boys of Fall’ in 2010, and he's still one 16 years later.

A pattern, not a fluke. Six of the ten longest gaps between #1s ended in the last two years. Bryan and [[Miranda Lambert]], whose eight-year wait ended with ‘Run’ in October 2025, closed theirs last year. That's six of the ten longest droughts in Hot 20 history ended in two years. For acts who have waited a long time, there hasn't been a better time to get back to the top.

headline: The CMAs and the Willboard Country Awards agree on 10 of 38 nominations. Ella Langley leads both
dek: Nine days before both shows, we lined up the two ballots. They share a leader, three albums and almost nothing else.
body: The CMA Awards and the 2026 Willboard Country Awards happen on the same night, November 18. Lay the two ballots side by side in the eight categories they share, and they match on just 10 of 38 nominations. The one thing they agree on is the leader. [[Ella Langley]] has nine CMA nominations, the most of anyone, and six Willboard nominations, also the most. Most of the difference comes from where each ballot looks. The CMAs are voted on by the industry and lean on radio. The Willboard ballot is Will's, and it follows the Hot 20.

Where they agree. Langley is the only act on both Entertainer of the Year lists, and her year on the Hot 20 explains why. Since last November she has charted six songs and taken four of them to #1: ‘Choosin' Texas’ for six weeks, ‘Be Her’ and ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ for three each, and ‘Hungover’ for one. ‘Choosin' Texas’ is a nominee for Single and Song of the Year on both ballots. Female Vocalist is the closest match, with Langley, [[Megan Moroney]] and [[Kacey Musgraves]] on both lists. Album of the Year shares three of five: Langley's Dandelion, Musgraves's Middle of Nowhere and [[Zach Top]]'s Ain't In It For My Health. Top is also the only Male Vocalist nominee on both.

The CMA's big names. The rest of the CMA Entertainer field is [[Luke Combs]], Cody Johnson, [[Chris Stapleton]] and [[Lainey Wilson]]. Three of them didn't chart on the Hot 20 at all this year. Combs and Stapleton both last charted in April 2024, Combs with ‘Where the Wild Things Are’ and Stapleton with ‘White Horse.’ Johnson has one Hot 20 entry ever, ‘With You I Am’ in 2017. Wilson is there with ‘Somewhere Over Laredo,’ which peaked at #5 and is up for Single of the Year at the CMAs. [[Miranda Lambert]] is the CMA's second-most nominated act with seven. She has 11 #1s on the Hot 20, but this year her only entry, ‘Two Things Can Be True,’ peaked at #18.

Will's picks the CMAs passed on. The Willboard ballot is full of acts who owned the Hot 20 and got nothing from the CMAs. [[Danielle Bradbery]]'s ‘Dent’ spent five weeks at #1 and is a Willboard nominee for Single of the Year. [[Kevin Powers]] has four Willboard nominations, including Male Vocalist and New Artist, on the strength of ‘Move On’ with [[Shaboozey]], a #1 that spent 29 weeks on the chart. [[Carly Pearce]] is a Willboard Entertainer nominee after charting five songs, led by ‘No Rain,’ two weeks at #1. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] charted three songs, including the #1 ‘Jesus, I'm Jealous,’ and is up for Female Vocalist, New Artist and Album. None of them has a CMA nomination in these categories.

Two different New Artist classes. This is where the ballots split completely. The CMA nominees are Avery Anna, Carter Faith, Emily Ann Roberts, Tucker Wetmore and [[Stephen Wilson Jr]]. Willboard's are [[Flatland Cavalry]], Mackenzie Carpenter, Kevin Powers, [[Ty Myers]] and [[Vincent Mason]]. Not one name overlaps. The groups split the same way. The CMA's Vocal Group and Vocal Duo fields have ten acts between them, and none of them charted on the Hot 20 this year. [[Lady A]] and [[Little Big Town]] were last there in 2024, and [[Brothers Osborne]] not since 2019. Will's three Duo/Group nominees, Flatland Cavalry, [[The Castellows]] and [[Maddie & Tae]], all charted this year.

One act the chart did get to first. Stephen Wilson Jr. is a CMA nominee for both Male Vocalist and New Artist, and his song ‘Gary’ is up for Song of the Year. Hot 20 readers knew him before this fall. ‘The Tunnel,’ his duet with [[Lori McKenna]], spent six weeks at #1 over the winter of 2024 and 2025.
We'll be watching both shows on November 18. Our predictions for the Willboard winners start Wednesday.

headline: Cassandra Coleman had the biggest year and Demi Lovato the busiest. Artist of the Year has room for both
dek: Our last nomination-predictions piece for the 2027 Pop Awards covers the top prize, then lays out our full predicted ballot in all six categories.
body: Artist of the Year is the one award that looks at a whole year instead of a single song. It asks who owned the Pop 10 from one November to the next, and the answer isn't always the act with the biggest hit. This year the case is unusually clear at the top and unusually crowded below it. [[Cassandra Coleman]] reached #1 with three different songs. [[Demi Lovato]] put six songs on the chart, more than anyone. Six other acts have a real claim on the last spots. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, and these are our predictions for the eight slots. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

What wins. Weeks at #1 are a decent guide here, but not a reliable one. The act with the most weeks at #1 in the eligibility year has won at seven of the 14 shows, including [[Ariana Grande]] at the 2015 show, [[Meghan Trainor]] at the 2016 show and Coleman at the 2024 show. The other seven went somewhere else, and three of them were real surprises. [[P!nk]] won at the 2014 show with two weeks at #1, while Macklemore & Ryan Lewis had nine. [[The Chainsmokers]] won at the 2018 show without a single #1 that year. They charted five songs and spent 32 weeks on the chart, and that was enough. Last year [[Nelly Furtado]] won with two #1s and five weeks on top, ahead of [[Sabrina Carpenter]]'s three #1s and seven weeks. Presence counts for a lot in this category. So does a defining song: Furtado's ‘Honesty’ also won Record of the Year.

Who gets in. The field is wide by design. Eight nominees since the 2020 show means room for acts with one big song, like [[Erika Vikman]] last year with ‘Ich Komme,’ and for acts who were simply always there, like [[Daughtry]] the year before with four charting songs and no #1. Meghan Trainor has been nominated seven times, more than anyone, and Ariana Grande and The Chainsmokers five times each. Repeat winners are common. The Chainsmokers have won four times and [[Kayla Rae]] twice.

The front-runner. Coleman's year is the strongest in the field by almost any measure. She had five songs on the chart and three of them reached #1: ‘Bite My Tongue,’ three weeks on top last November and December, ‘Maggie’ in July, and ‘End of Your Love’ in October. That's seven weeks at #1 in all, the most of any act, and 14 weeks in the Top 3, tied for the most. She had at least one song on the Pop 10 in 37 of the 51 chart weeks. When she won this award at the 2024 show, she swept all five categories she was eligible for. A second win would make her only the third act to win Artist of the Year more than once.

The busiest act. Demi Lovato doesn't have Coleman's #1s, but nobody charted more. Six of her songs made the Pop 10 this year: ‘Let You Go,’ ‘Here All Night,’ ‘Sorry to Myself,’ ‘In My Head,’ ‘Low Rise Jeans’ and ‘After Hours.’ Only ‘In My Head’ reached #1, for two weeks, but the other five all peaked at #2 or #3, and together they spent 12 weeks in the Top 3. Three of those songs were on the chart at the same time in late April. That's the 2018 Chainsmokers profile, and it won. Lovato is a four-time nominee who has never won this one.

The locks. [[Kim Petras]] and [[Chloe Tang]] each had two #1s. Petras had ‘Need for Speed’ for three weeks in the spring and ‘Brutalist’ for three in the summer, with ‘I Like Your Look’ reaching #5 before either, and she charted in 30 weeks. Tang's ‘Running on Blue’ with Casandra held #1 for two weeks last December, and ‘Obsexxed’ held it for four in the summer. Her 14 Top 3 weeks tie Coleman's. [[Katy Perry]] gets in on one long, slow hit: ‘Bandaids’ spent 17 weeks on the chart and three at #1, and ‘Watch It Burn’ added a Top 10 in July. She's a three-time nominee who has never won.

The likely. Kayla Rae is the hardest act in pop to leave off this ballot. She has four nominations and two wins, and this year she charted four songs in 26 weeks. ‘True’ peaked at #2 and spent seven weeks in the Top 3, and ‘It Wasn't Nothing’ debuted at #1 on October 29. [[Hilary Duff]] had three charting songs, led by ‘Weather for Tennis,’ four weeks at #1. [[Willa Ford]] had just one song, but ‘Love4Life’ spent four weeks at #1 and eight in the Top 3, and one-song acts have made this field before.

The bubble. [[Peach PRC]] is our first alternate. She charted three songs, including ‘Out Loud,’ three weeks at #1, and she was nominated last year. [[girlsweetvoiced]] has a strong case with ‘Cranberry,’ three weeks at #1 and seven in the Top 3, but it's her only charting song. [[Taylor Swift]] charted four songs in 24 weeks without one reaching the Top 3, which is a lot of presence and not much peak.

Snubs in waiting. Sabrina Carpenter won this award at the 2025 show and was nominated again last year, but this year she charted only two songs and neither reached #1. ‘Bring Your Love,’ her duet with [[Madonna]], peaked at #2. Meghan Trainor, a seven-time nominee, had two charting songs and one week in the Top 3. If either one makes the field, it will be on reputation.

The panel. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, keeps the list as it stands and picks Coleman to win: “Three #1s, seven weeks on top, 37 weeks on the chart. It's not close.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, swaps Willa Ford for Peach PRC: “One great single isn't a year. Peach PRC gave us three.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, keeps the list and picks Lovato to win: “Six songs. Every time I turned on the Pop 10, Demi was there.”
Our full predicted ballot. With nominations eight days away, here is everything we've predicted this week in one place. The first five categories come from this week's pieces, unchanged.
Artist of the Year: Cassandra Coleman, Demi Lovato, Kim Petras, Chloe Tang, Katy Perry, Kayla Rae, Hilary Duff, Willa Ford. Alternate: Peach PRC.

Record of the Year: ‘Obsexxed’ (Chloe Tang), ‘Brutalist’ (Kim Petras), ‘Love4Life’ (Willa Ford), ‘Bandaids’ (Katy Perry), ‘Cranberry’ ([[girlsweetvoiced]]), ‘Weather for Tennis’ (Hilary Duff), ‘End of Your Love’ (Cassandra Coleman), ‘Choke Me’ ([[Alexandra Căpitănescu]]). Alternate: ‘Stateside’ ([[Pink Pantheress]] and [[Zara Larsson]]).

Song of the Year: ‘Brutalist’ (Kim Petras), ‘Bandaids’ (Katy Perry), ‘Weather for Tennis’ (Hilary Duff), ‘Sue Me’ ([[Audrey Hobart]]), ‘Choke Me’ (Alexandra Căpitănescu), ‘Love4Life’ (Willa Ford), ‘End of Your Love’ (Cassandra Coleman), ‘Obsexxed’ (Chloe Tang). Alternate: ‘Cranberry’ (girlsweetvoiced).

Album of the Year: End of Your Love (Cassandra Coleman), luck... or something (Hilary Duff), Porcelain (Peach PRC), amanda (Willa Ford), Detour (Kim Petras), Fancy Some More? (Pink Pantheress), The Life of a Showgirl (Taylor Swift), Lovesweet (girlsweetvoiced). Alternate: Toy With Me (Meghan Trainor).

Best New Artist: Hilary Duff, Willa Ford, girlsweetvoiced, Alexandra Căpitănescu, [[Linda Lampenius]] and [[Pete Parkkonen]], Audrey Hobart, [[Holly Humberstone]], [[Avery Cochrane]]. Alternate: [[Adela]].

Foreign Language Song: ‘Liekinheitin’ (Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen), ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ ([[Karol G]]), ‘Ver Van M'n Bed’ ([[Roxy Dekker]]), ‘Ex Ex Ex’ ([[Aitana]] and [[Kenia Os]]), ‘Nân’ ([[Alis]]). Alternate: ‘Dai Dai’ ([[Shakira]] and [[Burna Boy]]).
Will's real nominees arrive on November 16. We'll be back that day to see how we did.

headline: No song held #1 for more than four weeks this year. That makes Record of the Year the most open race the Pop Awards have had
dek: Our fifth nomination-predictions piece for the 2027 Pop Awards looks at the hits themselves: how long they ran, how they climbed, how they sound, and our eight picks.
body: Record of the Year is the award for the hit. Song of the Year asks what a song says. Record asks how big the finished recording got and how it sounds coming out of the speakers. In most years the answer is obvious by November, because one song owns the chart. Not this year. For the first time in the history of the Pop Awards, no song in the eligibility year spent more than four weeks at #1, and four different songs are tied at exactly four. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, and these are our predictions for the eight slots. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

What wins. Record of the Year has the cleanest track record of any category Will hands out. The year's Year-End #1 has won it at 12 of the 14 shows, from [[Gotye]]'s ‘Somebody That I Used to Know’ at the first show in 2013 to [[Nelly Furtado]]'s ‘Honesty’ at the 2026 show. Both upsets went to the Year-End #2: [[The Chainsmokers]]' ‘High’ beat ‘Unholy’ at the 2023 show, and [[Ariana Grande]]'s ‘We Can't Be Friends’ beat ‘Espresso’ at the 2025 show. Every winner reached #1 during its eligibility year, and so did 84 of the 91 songs ever nominated.

Staying power beats a hot streak. Weeks at #1 are a weaker guide than you'd think. The winner led or shared the lead in weeks at #1 at only eight of the 14 shows. What matters more is how long a record stays near the top. ‘Honesty’ won last year with four weeks at #1 against [[Erika Vikman]]'s seven for ‘Ich Komme,’ because ‘Honesty’ spent 18 weeks in the Top 3 and stayed on the chart for 24. At the 2018 show, [[Demi Lovato]]'s ‘Sorry Not Sorry’ won with a single week at #1, beating ‘Perfect Strangers’ and its five, because no song that year spent longer in the Top 3. A record that sits at #2 and #3 for months tends to finish the year higher than one that burns bright at #1 and fades.

The most crowded year at the top. That's why this year is so hard to call. The eligibility year runs from last year's nominations to the chart of November 12, and so far 21 different songs have reached #1. That ties the 2015 and 2018 shows for the second-most ever, behind the 2014 show's 22. The longest stay on top is four weeks, shared by [[Chloe Tang]]'s ‘Obsexxed,’ [[Willa Ford]]'s ‘Love4Life,’ [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ and [[Alexandra Căpitănescu]]'s ‘Choke Me.’ The last time no song reached even six weeks was the year before the 2018 show, when the longest run was five, and that's the year a one-week #1 won. Twenty of those 21 #1s are eligible. [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘Bite My Tongue’ was already nominated last year, and no song is nominated twice.

The front-runner. Chloe Tang's ‘Obsexxed’ has the best all-around year. It debuted at #5 on May 7, slipped as low as #10, and took eight weeks to reach #1. Then it stayed four weeks and spent nine weeks in the Top 3, tied for the most in the field, across 15 weeks on the chart. That climb is the profile of a Record winner, the slow build that keeps a song in the conversation for a whole season. Tang also has ‘Running on Blue’ with Casandra, which debuted at #1 last December and stayed two weeks, but no act has ever had two Record nominees in the same year, and ‘Obsexxed’ is the one that will carry her name.

The locks. [[Kim Petras]]'s ‘Brutalist’ matches ‘Obsexxed’ with nine weeks in the Top 3 and adds three weeks at #1 over a 14-week run. It's the year's sharpest-sounding single, what one critic called “really snappy synthpop,” a bright, catchy beat carrying a song about a childhood memory, from an album executive produced by Petras and Margo XS. Willa Ford's ‘Love4Life’ came in at #10 in January and was #1 by its third week. It stayed four weeks and spent eight in the Top 3. Ford co-produced it with Gustav Afsahi and Jonathan Bluth. She wrote it as a love song to her husband, and then, as she put it, “We decided to put a fun dance beat to that song.” It comes from amanda, her first album in more than two decades, and it sounds like a record made by someone who missed the dance floor.

The slow burner. [[Katy Perry]]'s ‘Bandaids’ took the longest road of any contender. It entered at #8 the week of November 13, 2025, the first week of the eligibility year, and sat between #8 and #9 for seven weeks before it moved. Then it climbed 5-2-1 and held #1 for three weeks. Its 17 weeks on the chart are the most of any song in the field. The sound is a throwback: a pop rock ballad at 94 beats per minute with what reviewers called “metallic, shimmery guitars,” produced by Justin Tranter, Sean Cook, Russ Chell and Eren Cannata. Clash heard an echo of the pop rock ballads on One of the Boys, and patience like that has been rewarded here before.

The fast starters. Three contenders debuted at #1, which is the opposite profile. Hilary Duff's ‘Weather for Tennis,’ the opening track on luck... or something, arrived at #1 the week of March 5 and stayed four weeks. Matthew Koma and Brian Phillips produced the album, which Rolling Stone called a “shimmering, synth-pop comeback,” and the single moves quick and light, like the back-and-forth it describes. Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me’ is the only real rock record in the race, heavy guitars and an electronic edge, and it went to #1 the week after Romania's Eurovision final, where it placed third with 296 points, the country's highest score ever. It held #1 for four weeks, but it was gone after six. [[Peach PRC]]'s ‘Out Loud’ did the same thing at Christmas: three weeks at #1, eight weeks total. History says debuts like these are dangerous to bet against and easy to overrate. They lead the chart, then they leave it.

The late arrivals. [[girlsweetvoiced]]'s ‘Cranberry,’ from the debut album Lovesweet, is the summer's quiet surprise: a breathy, near-whispered vocal over clean electronic production that somehow climbed 4-4-3-2-1 and held #1 for three weeks, with seven weeks in the Top 3. Cassandra Coleman's ‘End of Your Love’ is the newest contender. It debuted at #6 on October 1, jumped to #1 the next week and stayed three weeks. Coleman won this award at the 2024 show with ‘Habit,’ and the voters know her name. The question is whether six weeks of chart history is enough. [[Kayla Rae]]'s ‘It Wasn't Nothing’ debuted at #1 two weeks ago and is still there. With one chart left in the eligibility year, it has the least time of anyone to make its case.

The bubble. [[Pink Pantheress]] and [[Zara Larsson]]'s ‘Stateside’ is the best candidate outside our eight. It spent 14 weeks on the chart and two at #1, a steady single that never quite owned the top. Kayla Rae's ‘True’ never reached #1, peaking at #2, but it spent seven weeks in the Top 3, more than ‘Weather for Tennis’ or ‘Choke Me.’ That would be enough in most years, but only seven non-#1 songs have ever been nominated, and there are 20 eligible #1s to choose from this time.

Snubs in waiting. Someone good is going to miss. With 20 eligible #1s and eight slots, at least 12 songs that topped the chart won't be nominated. That list will likely include Kim Petras's ‘Need for Speed,’ three weeks at #1 but only four on the chart, and [[Linda Lampenius]] and Pete Parkkonen's ‘Liekinheitin,’ which spent six weeks in the Top 3. The hardest cut is between ‘Choke Me’ and ‘Out Loud,’ two records with nearly the same run. We give ‘Choke Me’ the edge for its extra week at #1, and because no other contender sounds like it.

The panel. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, keeps the list as it stands and picks ‘Obsexxed’ to win: “Nine weeks in the Top 3 and four at #1. Nobody else has both.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, swaps ‘End of Your Love’ for ‘Stateside’: “Six weeks isn't a year. Give me the record that was around in February and still sounded fresh in May.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, swaps ‘Choke Me’ for Kayla Rae's ‘True’: “It never hit #1, and it never left my car either.”

ballot.title: Our predicted nominees: Record of the Year
ballot.note: First alternate: ‘Stateside’ by [[Pink Pantheress]] and [[Zara Larsson]]. Nominees are announced November 16.

headline: Song of the Year rewards what a song says. Kim Petras's ‘Brutalist’ says the most this year
dek: Our fourth nomination-predictions piece for the 2027 Pop Awards looks at the writing: the stories, the lines and the craft behind this year's contenders, and our eight picks.
body: Song of the Year is the songwriter's award. Record of the Year rewards the finished recording and how big it got. This one asks what the song says and how well it's built. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, and these are our predictions for the eight slots. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

What wins. The chart gets a song into the conversation, but the winners lean on the writing. Eight of the 14 winners weren't even nominated for Record. [[Kelly Clarkson]] won at the 2017 show with ‘It's Quiet Uptown,’ Lin-Manuel Miranda's song about grief from Hamilton. [[Ke$ha]]'s ‘Praying,’ a song about finding peace after being hurt, won the next year without a Record nomination. Two winners, [[The Chainsmokers]]' ‘Everybody Hates Me’ and [[Kayla Rae]]'s ‘Get Close,’ never reached #1 at all. A clear story and a line you remember can beat a bigger hit with less to say.

The ground rules. Most nominees still come from the top of the chart: since the field grew to eight in 2020, 41 of the 56 reached #1. No act has ever had two Song nominees in the same year, so [[Kim Petras]], [[Chloe Tang]] and [[Cassandra Coleman]] each get one shot. And no song is nominated twice, which rules out Coleman's ‘Bite My Tongue’ and [[Demi Lovato]]'s ‘Let You Go’ from last year's field.

The front-runner. Kim Petras's ‘Brutalist’ is the best-written song of the year. It's built on one childhood memory: Petras and her father, an architect, driving past a brutalist post office in Hamburg on the way to her hormone-therapy appointments. The building was later torn down. “There was a building there / And it was Brutalist,” she opens, almost flatly, and the hook, “I guess I ruined it,” answers the people who say she ruined her life by turning it into a story about a building nobody else thought was worth saving. “It's the story of my dad and I driving around in Germany to get my hormone therapy when I was a kid,” she told The FADER. It also spent three weeks at #1.

Heartbreak, written plainly. [[Katy Perry]]'s ‘Bandaids’ is the most direct song she has put out in years. The title carries the whole idea, small fixes on a broken heart, and the first line, “Hand to God, I promised I tried,” starts the argument before the chorus arrives. She wrote it with Justin Tranter and four others and said she “struggled for months” over whether to release it. [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ turns a couple stuck in the same fight into a tennis match. The chorus keeps the ball going back and forth, the pre-chorus ends by putting “the ball in your court,” and the best line comes early: “I'm a seasoned apologist / For the people who I love.”

The risk-takers. [[Audrey Hobart]] wrote ‘Sue Me’ on her own, one of the first songs she ever wrote alone, about a night out with an ex she knew was still in love with her. The hook, “Sue me, I wanna be wanted,” is a shrug and a confession in six words. It spent one week at #1, which is the profile of more than one past winner. [[Alexandra Căpitănescu]]'s ‘Choke Me’ is the boldest pick. Its title drew criticism before Eurovision, and she answered that the lyrics are “about taking back control over anxiety and emotions that are choking you.” It builds from quiet verses into a chorus that won't let go, and it debuted at #1 and stayed four weeks, the same opening run as ‘It's Quiet Uptown.’

Love songs, two ways. [[Willa Ford]] wrote ‘Love4Life’ with Gustav Afsahi and Jonathan Bluth about her husband, then, in her words, “put a fun dance beat to that song.” A sincere love song dressed for the dance floor is harder to pull off than it sounds. Cassandra Coleman, who won this award at the 2024 show with ‘Habit,’ comes from the other side with ‘End of Your Love,’ a song about bracing for a partner to leave. Its refrain, “I keep waiting for the end of your love,” keeps circling back until the song fades on it.

The last slot. Chloe Tang's ‘Obsexxed’ gets in on the strength of its year: four weeks at #1, tied for the longest stay on top, and 15 weeks on the chart. First in line if he goes another way is [[girlsweetvoiced]]'s ‘Cranberry,’ three weeks at #1. Kayla Rae, already a three-time Song nominee, has ‘True’ and her new #1 ‘It Wasn't Nothing’ in the running.

The panel. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, swaps ‘Sue Me’ for ‘Cranberry’: “Three weeks at #1 is hard to leave off, whatever the lyric sheet says.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, keeps the list as it stands and picks ‘Brutalist’ to win: “It's a song about a building that's really about a life. That's songwriting.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, swaps ‘Obsexxed’ for Kayla Rae's ‘True’: “Kayla Rae writes the songs I send to my friends.”

ballot.title: Our predicted nominees: Song of the Year
ballot.note: First alternate: ‘Cranberry’ by [[girlsweetvoiced]]. Nominees are announced November 16.

headline: Cassandra Coleman leads the Album of the Year race, and one-hit albums could fill half the field
dek: Our third nomination-predictions piece for the 2027 Pop Awards covers what puts an album in the field, the records that look safe, and who's fighting for the last spots.
body: Album of the Year goes to a body of work, but on the Willboard Pop Awards that body of work is judged by how it charted. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, and these are our predictions for the eight slots. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

What it takes. Since the field grew to eight in 2020, about two-thirds of the nominees we can match to the Pop 10 had a #1 in their eligibility year, and about two-thirds had at least two hits. One huge single can be enough, though: more than a dozen nominees got in on a single hit, among them [[Nelly Furtado]]'s 7 last year, carried by ‘Honesty.’ Release year doesn't matter much either. [[Gwen Stefani]]'s Bouquet, last year's winner, came out in 2024 and won on the strength of two #1s in 2025.

One shot per album. Like the Grammys, the Pop Awards nominate an album only once. That rules out the year's busiest album: [[Demi Lovato]]'s It's Not That Deep charted six songs in this window, including ‘In My Head’ with two weeks at #1, but it was nominated last year. [[Sabrina Carpenter]]'s Man's Best Friend is out for the same reason.

The locks. [[Cassandra Coleman]], who won in 2024 with Coming of Age, has the strongest album of the year on paper. End of Your Love has five Pop 10 hits in the window, three of them #1s (‘Bite My Tongue,’ ‘Maggie’ and the title track), for seven weeks on top in all. [[Hilary Duff]]'s luck... or something has three hits, led by ‘Weather for Tennis’ and its four weeks at #1. [[Peach PRC]]'s Porcelain has ‘Out Loud,’ three weeks at #1, plus ‘Eucalyptus’ in the top 5.

Likely. Then come the single-hit albums whose hits were too big to ignore: [[Willa Ford]]'s amanda, with ‘Love4Life’ (four weeks at #1, 13 on the chart); [[Kim Petras]]'s Detour, with ‘Brutalist’ (three weeks at #1, 14 on the chart); and [[Pink Pantheress]]'s Fancy Some More?, with ‘Stateside’ and [[Zara Larsson]] (two weeks at #1, 14 on the chart).

The bubble. Two slots are left, and the cases go different ways. [[Taylor Swift]]'s The Life of a Showgirl has four hits this year, ‘Honey,’ ‘Opalite,’ ‘Elizabeth Taylor’ and ‘Patient Zero,’ but none got higher than #4. [[girlsweetvoiced]]'s Lovesweet has one song, ‘Cranberry,’ which spent three weeks at #1. [[Meghan Trainor]]'s Toy With Me has ‘Still Don't Care’ (nine weeks, peaking at #2) and ‘Shimmer.’ [[Harry Styles]]'s Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally. has three hits, topped by ‘Aperture’ at #4.

Snubs-in-waiting. [[Karol G]] and [[Roxy Dekker]] both had #1s this fall, but each from an album with only one hit, and theirs arrived late in the window. [[Olivia Rodrigo]], [[Ariana Grande]] and [[Adela]] each have two Top 10 hits from new albums, and none of those hits went higher than #4.

The panel. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, takes the three locks, the three likely picks, Swift and Lovesweet: “Four hits in one window is hard to leave out, and so are three weeks at #1.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, swaps Willa Ford for Harry Styles: “That's the most complete album in the group, front to back.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, swaps Swift for Meghan Trainor: “‘Still Don't Care’ was on every playlist I made this year.”

ballot.title: Our predicted nominees: Album of the Year
items: The Life of a Showgirl by [[Taylor Swift]]
ballot.note: First alternate: Toy With Me by [[Meghan Trainor]]. Nominees are announced November 16.

headline: Ninety-one Best New Artist nominees, and none has been nominated twice. That's bad news for Chloe Tang
dek: Our second nomination-predictions piece for the 2027 Pop Awards: what it has taken to make the New Artist field, the seven acts who look safe, and a fight for the eighth slot.
body: Best New Artist is the Pop Awards category with the most turnover by design. There have been 14 shows and 91 nominees: five a year through 2019 and eight a year since 2020. Not one act has been nominated twice. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, and these are our predictions. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

Arrive during the year. The clearest pattern is timing. Of the 88 nominees with Pop 10 history, 81 had their very first Pop 10 entry inside the eligibility year. The other seven had debuted within seven months of it. [[Meghan Trainor]], [[Chappell Roan]] and [[Ava Max]] all arrived just before their window opened. This year the window covers everything charted since last year's nominations. The November 5 and November 12 charts still count.

‘New’ means new to the Pop 10. The field has never been only for unknowns. [[Loreen]] had already won Eurovision when she was nominated in 2024, and [[Kelsea Ballerini]] was a Hot 20 star by then. [[Erika Vikman]] was nominated last year after years of hits in Finland. What matters is the act's first year on this chart.

A #1 helps, but it isn't required. Since the field grew to eight in 2020, 21 of the 54 nominees we can match to the chart had reached #1 in their eligibility year, and 11 more peaked at #2. Nominees have peaked as low as #10: [[Dove Cameron]] made the 2023 field with exactly that. Winning is different. Eleven of the 13 winners we can match had a #1 in their year, and the exceptions were [[Cardi B]] (#2) and [[Jax]] (#3).

The locks. Five acts topped the Pop 10 in their first year. [[Hilary Duff]] was a pop star before this chart existed, but she had never been on it before January. Since then she has charted three songs, and ‘Weather for Tennis’ debuted at #1 and stayed there four weeks. [[Willa Ford]]'s ‘Love4Life’ spent four straight weeks at #1 and 13 on the chart. [[girlsweetvoiced]]'s ‘Cranberry’ climbed for four weeks, then held #1 for three. [[Alexandra Căpitănescu]]'s ‘Choke Me’ is sung in English, so it can't compete in Foreign Language Song, but here its four weeks at #1 make her a lock. [[Linda Lampenius]] and [[Pete Parkkonen]]'s ‘Liekinheitin’ spent six of its eight weeks in the top 3.

Likely. [[Audrey Hobart]]'s ‘Sue Me’ reached #1 in its third week and then spent three weeks at #2. [[Holly Humberstone]] never got to #1, but ‘Cruel World’ spent ten weeks on the chart, five of them at #3 or higher. Last year's field had room for acts that peaked at #3 and below, so a #2 with that kind of staying power should be safe.

The bubble. Those seven leave one slot. [[Avery Cochrane]]'s ‘Shapeshifting on a Saturday Night’ spent three weeks at #3. [[Adela]] has two Top 10 hits since August, ‘Ain't in LA’ and ‘Nicole Kidman.’ [[Alis]] spent both of her weeks at #3 with ‘Nân.’ [[Disco Lines]] spent five weeks at #4 with ‘No Broke Boys.’ [[Casandra]] reached #1 as the featured voice on [[Chloe Tang]]'s ‘Running on Blue,’ which may count for less than a hit of her own.

The snubs-in-waiting. Under the rules, an act can be nominated again for New Artist. In practice it has never happened, and that's the biggest question in this category. Chloe Tang was a 2025 nominee, and this year she had two #1s and six weeks on top, a bigger year than most of the field. [[Roxy Dekker]] and [[Aitana]] were nominated last year, and both are back with big hits. If history holds, all three sit this one out. Last year's winner, [[Peach PRC]], is still charting, but she can't win the category again.

The panel's predicted nominees. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, takes the five #1 acts, Hobart, Humberstone and Avery Cochrane: “Three weeks at #3 is the best résumé on the bubble.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, keeps the first seven and swaps in Adela: “Two Top 10s in two months says this isn't a one-off.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, gives the last slot to Chloe Tang: “The rules say she can come back. Six weeks at #1 says she should.”

ballot.title: Our predicted nominees: Best New Artist
ballot.note: First alternate: [[Adela]]. Nominees are announced November 16.

headline: Foreign Language Song turns two: three songs look like locks, and the year's biggest Eurovision hit isn't eligible
dek: The 2027 Pop Awards nominations arrive November 16. Our first prediction piece looks at what earned a nomination in the category's first year and who fits that mold now.
body: Foreign Language Song of the Year joined the Willboard Pop Awards at the 2026 show, so it has exactly one year of history. That year still tells us a lot. The 2027 nominees come out on November 16, the same day as the Grammy nominations, and these are our predictions for the five slots. They are predictions only. Will picks the nominees, and we haven't seen them.

What got in last year. The first field was [[Erika Vikman]]'s ‘Ich Komme,’ [[Shkodra Elektonike]]'s ‘Zjerm,’ [[Roxy Dekker]]'s ‘Ga Dan,’ [[Aitana]]'s ‘Superestrella’ and [[Kaj]]'s ‘Bara Bada Bastu.’ Three of them reached #1, ‘Superestrella’ peaked at #2, and ‘Bara Bada Bastu’ spent three weeks at #3. Nothing that peaked at #4 or lower made the cut: [[Væb]]'s ‘Róa’ and Roxy Dekker's ‘Hoe Het Is’ both stalled at #4, and Aitana's ‘En el Centro De La Cama’ and ‘Cómo Pasó’ by [[Ela Taubert]] and [[Joe Jonas]] stopped at #5. The field also held one song per act. Roxy Dekker had two #1s that year, and only ‘Ga Dan,’ with four weeks on top, got in; ‘Jouw Idee’ spent one week there and missed. The winner, ‘Ich Komme,’ had seven weeks at #1, the most in the field.

The window. This year's eligible songs are the ones that charted on the Pop 10 after last year's nominations. Two more charts, November 5 and November 12, still count. ‘Superestrella’ charted into the new window, but it can't return because no song is nominated twice.

The locks. Three non-English songs reached #1 this year. [[Linda Lampenius]] and [[Pete Parkkonen]]'s ‘Liekinheitin,’ Finland's Eurovision entry, sung in Finnish, debuted at #2 in May, spent four weeks there, took #1 for a week, and finished with eight weeks on the chart, six of them in the top 3. [[Karol G]]'s Spanish-language ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ reached #1 in its second week and has spent four weeks in the top 3. Roxy Dekker's ‘Ver Van M'n Bed’ hit #1 in its second week and has spent five of its six weeks in the top 3. Those two are still on the chart, and a nomination would make Dekker the category's first two-time nominee.

Likely: Aitana, but with which song? If the one-song-per-act pattern holds, Aitana gets a single slot. ‘Ex Ex Ex’ with [[Kenia Os]] has the better résumé so far: it peaked at #2 and spent seven weeks on the chart. ‘6 of Febrero’ has peaked at #3 and is still charting, five weeks in. Either one would give Aitana her second straight nomination.

The bubble. The fifth slot is the real race. [[Alis]]'s ‘Nân,’ Albania's Eurovision entry, sung entirely in Albanian, spent both of its weeks at #3. That fits last year's line exactly, and Albania sent ‘Zjerm’ to the field last year. [[Shakira]] and [[Burna Boy]]'s World Cup anthem ‘Dai Dai’ also peaked at #3, but it spent only one of its three weeks there, and it was written in five languages, English among them, so it may not count as a foreign-language song. Denmark's ‘Før vi går hjem’ by [[Søren Torpegaard Lund]], sung entirely in Danish, lasted four weeks but peaked at #4, the spot where ‘Róa’ and ‘Hoe Het Is’ fell short last year.

Not eligible. The biggest Eurovision hit on the Pop 10 this year can't be nominated. [[Alexandra Căpitănescu]]'s ‘Choke Me,’ Romania's third-place entry, debuted at #1 and spent four weeks there, but it's sung in English. The contest winner, [[Dara]]'s ‘Bangaranga,’ is mostly in English too, and it charted for a single week at #5.

The panel's predicted nominees. Mitzi Tallyho, going by the data, picks the songs with the highest peaks and the most weeks in the top 3: “‘Liekinheitin,’ ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba,’ ‘Ver Van M'n Bed,’ ‘Ex Ex Ex’ and ‘Nân.’ Two weeks at #3 beats one, and last year #3 was enough.” Sebastian Crescendo, going by craft, swaps in ‘6 of Febrero’ for Aitana and ‘Før vi går hjem’ for ‘Nân’: “It's the best-written song in the bunch, and one spot lower on the chart shouldn't keep it out.” Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, going by heart, keeps ‘Ex Ex Ex’ and gives the last slot to ‘Dai Dai’: “That was the sound of the whole summer. If it counts, it's in.”

ballot.title: Our predicted nominees: Foreign Language Song
ballot.note: First alternate: ‘Dai Dai’ by [[Shakira]] and [[Burna Boy]]. Nominees are announced November 16.

linkText: Watch the five New Artist nominees race
headline: No act has won New Artist of the Year without a Hot 20 #1. Two of this year's five nominees don't have one
dek: Sixteen Country Awards shows, sixteen New Artist winners, and every one of them had already topped the chart. Here's what else the history says about the 2026 field.
body: New Artist of the Year is the hardest Country Awards category to call, because the nominees have so little history to judge. But the winners have one thing in common. Every New Artist winner since the first show in 2010, from David Nail to [[Zach Top]], had already reached #1 on the Hot 20 by show night. Sixteen shows, sixteen winners, no exceptions.

More #1s usually wins. Counting only songs that reached #1 before each show, the winner had the most #1s in its field, or shared the lead, at 15 of the 16 shows. The lone exception was 2014, when [[Jennifer Nettles]] had two #1s to [[Jamie Lynn Spears]]'s one and Spears won anyway.

Weeks at #1 don't break ties. Eight times the leaders were tied on #1s, and the nominee with more weeks on top won only half of them. [[Ingrid Andress]] spent five weeks at #1 to [[Gabby Barrett]]'s three before the 2020 show, and Barrett won. [[Ashley Cooke]] had two weeks on top to [[Ella Langley]]'s one in 2024, and Langley won. Coming back helps, though: five of the 16 winners had been nominated in the category the year before, including Barrett and Zach Top.

‘New’ is relative. The category has never been only for unknowns. The 2014 field included both halves of [[Sugarland]], [[Jennifer Nettles]] and [[Kristian Bush]], whose duo already had eight Hot 20 hits and three #1s. The winner that year was [[Jamie Lynn Spears]], who had been a household name since her Nickelodeon days on ‘Zoey 101.’ [[Lady A]]'s [[Hillary Scott]] and [[Charles Kelley]] were both nominated in 2016, with 15 Lady A hits and six #1s already behind them. [[Kimberly Perry]] was nominated in 2023, twelve years after [[The Band Perry]] won the category, and the very first winner, David Nail, came back to the field in 2019 fronting David Nail & the Well Ravens. [[Chris Stapleton]] had spent years as a Nashville songwriter and the lead singer of The SteelDrivers before he won in 2017. None of the nominees who arrived from an act that already had Hot 20 hits has won. Voters have been happy to nominate a familiar name and then give the award to someone newer to the chart.
The 2026 field. Here's where the five nominees stand going into Nov. 18:

[[Mackenzie Carpenter]] is the only nominee with more than one #1. ‘I Wish You Would’ spent five weeks on top in 2025, the year she earned her first New Artist nomination, and ‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’ added a sixth week this year. All four of her Hot 20 entries have reached the top 2, and she has 75 weeks on the chart, the most in the field.

[[Flatland Cavalry]] reached #1 for two weeks with ‘A Life Where We Work Out,’ a duet with [[Kaitlin Butts]], who was a New Artist nominee herself in 2022. [[Kevin Powers]] has one #1, ‘Move On’ with [[Shaboozey]], and it was a slow one: it took 27 weeks to get from its debut to the top, tied for the third-longest wait in Hot 20 history.

[[Ty Myers]] and [[Vincent Mason]] have each peaked at #2, Myers with ‘Message to You’ and Mason with ‘Wish You Well.’ Mason and Carpenter are both back from last year's field, which Zach Top won. If Myers or Mason wins, it will be a first for the category.
History points to Carpenter, but history doesn't vote. The winners will be revealed on Nov. 18, the same night as the CMA Awards.

linkText: Watch ‘Pink Pony Club’ make its comeback
headline: ‘Pink Pony Club’ left the Pop 10 for nine weeks and came back at #1. No other song has done that
dek: Most Pop 10 #1s get there fast. A few took the long way: they fell off the chart, sat out for months, or spent a whole season climbing. Here are the longest roads to the top.
body: Most Pop 10 #1s don't wait long. The typical chart-topper gets there by about its fourth week. A handful took the scenic route, and the three slowest all did it the same way: they left the chart, stayed away for months, and then came back stronger.

The record: ‘Demons.’ [[Imagine Dragons]]' ‘Demons’ debuted at #8 on June 13, 2013, held there a second week, and then vanished for 21 weeks. It came back at #8 on Nov. 21, jumped to #4, and reached #1 on Dec. 5, 25 weeks after its debut. It stayed on top for three weeks. No Pop 10 #1 has waited longer.

Runner-up: ‘Pompeii.’ [[Bastille]] followed the same script a few months later. ‘Pompeii’ debuted at #6 on Oct. 17, 2013, peaked at #4, and dropped off after five weeks. It sat out 14 weeks, re-entered at #2 on Feb. 27, 2014, and took over #1 the next week, on March 6. That was 20 weeks after its debut, and it also held #1 for three weeks.

The one-of-a-kind comeback. [[Chappell Roan]]'s ‘Pink Pony Club’ debuted at #2 on Oct. 31, 2024 and spent nine weeks in the Top 5 without reaching #1. Then it disappeared. Nine weeks later, on March 6, 2025, it returned at #1: exactly 11 years to the day after ‘Pompeii’ first reached the top. It held on for four weeks. ‘Pink Pony Club’ is the only song in Pop 10 history to re-enter at #1, and no song on the Hot 20 has done it either.

The long, steady climbs. The Pop 10 record for continuous weeks on the chart before reaching #1 belongs to [[Meghan Trainor]], and she holds second place too. ‘Nice to Meet Ya’ with Nicki Minaj debuted at #10 on Feb. 6, 2020 and climbed for 15 straight weeks before reaching #1 on May 21; it held the top spot for two weeks. A year earlier, ‘All the Ways’ debuted at #5 on Feb. 21, 2019 and spent 14 weeks between #3 and #7 before a one-week stay at #1 on May 30. Both of Trainor's slow climbs reached #1 in late May.

Just behind them: [[Lewis Capaldi]]'s ‘Someone You Loved’ reached #1 in its 14th week in 2019. P!nk and Nate Ruess's ‘Just Give Me A Reason’ and [[Fall Out Boy]]'s ‘My Songs Know What You Did In The Dark’ both got there in their 13th week in 2013.

On the other chart. Country radio moves more slowly, and so does the Hot 20. Sara Evans's ‘A Little Bit Stronger’ holds that chart's record: 33 weeks passed between its debut in September 2010 and its one week at #1 in May 2011.

linkText: Watch Dustin Lynch vs Ashley Cooke
headline: Dustin Lynch's new album brings in Ashley Cooke. On the Hot 20, she has been the steadier hitmaker
dek: ‘Clean Slate’ arrived Oct. 30 with Cooke on ‘How You Been,’ and her holiday EP follows next week. Their Willboard records could hardly be more different.
body: [[Dustin Lynch]] released his seventh studio album, ‘Clean Slate,’ on Oct. 30 through BBR Music Group/BMG Nashville. It has 12 songs, led by the single ‘Made In A Bottle,’ and track five is ‘How You Been,’ a duet with [[Ashley Cooke]] produced by Ross Copperman. Cooke has her own release coming next Friday, Nov. 6: ‘wrapped,’ a five-song holiday EP on Big Loud Records with two originals and three Christmas standards.

Lynch: a fast start, then a long gap. His label counts ten country radio #1s, but only three of his songs have reached the Hot 20. ‘Cowboys And Angels’ entered at #20 on July 12, 2012, climbed to #2 and stayed for 16 weeks. ‘Wild In Your Smile’ spent a single week at #20 in January 2014. After that he was gone from the chart for more than ten years.

Then a #1 as a guest. He returned as the featured voice on [[Madeline Merlo]]'s ‘Broken Heart Thing,’ which entered at #19 on Nov. 14, 2024. It reached #1 on Feb. 6, 2025, spent four weeks there and stayed on the chart for 17 weeks. That's still Lynch's only Hot 20 #1, and he got it on someone else's single.

Cooke: never far from the top. Cooke's first entry, ‘Running Back,’ arrived in January 2023, and she has put eight songs on the Hot 20 since then. Every one of them reached the top 12. ‘Your Place’ gave her a first #1 in July 2024, holding the top spot for two weeks. ‘Swear Words’ followed it to #1 in January 2026 and stayed for three. Her duet with Colbie Caillat, ‘Mean Girl,’ peaked at #7.

Where she stands now. Her latest, ‘High School Sweetheart,’ entered at #20 on Sept. 3 and peaked at #12. It was at #14 on the Oct. 29 chart, its eighth week. That's two Hot 20 #1s for Cooke in less than four years on the chart, against one for Lynch in fourteen.

‘How You Been’ is the first time the two have shared a song. Whether it reaches the Hot 20 is up to Will's listening. In the meantime, you can race their careers against each other on the new Chart Videos page.

headline: Weeks at #1 don't decide Entertainer of the Year. Weeks in the top 5 almost always do
dek: The act with the most top 5 weeks has won 14 of the last 16 Entertainer races. The act with the most weeks at #1 has won only seven.
body: Entertainer of the Year is the biggest award at the Willboard Country Awards, and the hardest to call from the chart. Is it about #1s, weeks on top, or just being everywhere? We went back through all 16 Entertainer races from 2010 to 2025 and compared every nominee's Hot 20 record in the 12 months before each show, from November through October. We looked at five measures: #1 hits, weeks at #1, weeks in the top 5, chart entries and total weeks on the chart. Where an act had more than one song charting, each song's weeks count separately.

The headline number. The nominee with the most top 5 weeks has won Entertainer 14 times in 16 years. Most #1 hits comes next, but only when you count ties: the winner had the most #1s, or shared the lead, 12 times. Weeks at #1, the stat that sounds the most important, is the weakest. The nominee who spent the most weeks on top has won only seven times.

Wins without the most weeks on top. [[Carrie Underwood]], the only three-time winner, shows the pattern best. In 2023 she won with just two weeks at #1, while [[Kip Moore]] had nine. What she did have was 26 top 5 weeks, the most in the field. [[Leann Rimes]] beat [[Craig Campbell]] in 2014 with 25 top 5 weeks to his 18, even though Campbell spent 12 weeks at #1 to her 10. In 2022, [[Carly Pearce]] led with 24 top 5 weeks and won, while [[Runaway June]] had the most weeks at #1 with seven. Last year [[Ella Langley]] won with only three weeks at #1, against Pearce's eight, because she had 35 top 5 weeks to Pearce's 29.

The two exceptions. In 2017, Little Big Town led the field with 18 top 5 weeks, but Miranda Lambert won with 16. She had the most weeks at #1 that year with 10, so she still led on another major measure. The real upset came in 2015. Rimes won with just five top 5 weeks, the fewest in the field, and one week at #1. Kacey Musgraves led with 17 top 5 weeks without a single #1, and Tyler Farr had nine weeks on top. Nothing on the chart points to Rimes that year.

This year's field. Here's how the 2026 nominees stack up from November 2025 through the Oct. 22 chart. Ella Langley has 38 top 5 weeks, four #1s and 13 weeks at #1. [[Megan Moroney]] has 28 top 5 weeks, two #1s and eight weeks on top. [[Kacey Musgraves]] has 25 top 5 weeks, two #1s and seven weeks on top. [[Zach Top]] has 21, two and seven. Carly Pearce has seven, one and two.

By the measure that has called 14 of the last 16 races, Langley leads the field. But the stat said the same about Musgraves in 2015, and Rimes won anyway. We'll find out on Nov. 18, the night the CMA Awards air.

linkText: See every song that debuted at #1
headline: Thirty-one songs have debuted at #1 on the Pop 10. A record six of them arrived in 2025
dek: Some opened at the top and stayed for months, and one lasted a single week. Here's the history of the Pop 10's instant #1s. Updated Oct. 30 with Kayla Rae's ‘It Wasn't Nothing.’
body: Since the Pop 10 launched on Oct. 27, 2011, 31 songs have entered the chart at #1. That leaves out the launch week itself, when every song on the chart was new. Drake and Rihanna's ‘Take Care’ was the first, on Feb. 9, 2012. The most recent is [[Kayla Rae]]'s ‘It Wasn't Nothing,’ which opened at #1 on Oct. 29, 2026, the week after this story first ran.

The longest stay. [[Bruno Mars]] set the bar early. ‘Locked Out of Heaven’ debuted at #1 on Oct. 18, 2012 and stayed there for its first 11 weeks. No other song that debuted on top has come close: the next-longest opening streaks are six weeks, by [[Macklemore]] and Ryan Lewis's ‘Can't Hold Us’ (2013), [[The Chainsmokers]] and Halsey's ‘Closer’ (2016), Julia Michaels's ‘Worst In Me’ (2017) and The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ (2022). ‘Locked Out of Heaven’ is also the third-longest-running #1 of any kind on the Pop 10, behind only ‘Somebody That I Used To Know’ (15 weeks) and ‘Habit’ (14).

Short visits. Opening at #1 doesn't guarantee a long run. [[Meghan Trainor]]'s ‘No Excuses’ debuted on top on March 8, 2018 and fell to #2 the next week; it's the only one of the first 30 that spent just one week at #1. Logic's ‘1-800-273-8255,’ with Alessia Cara and Khalid, held #1 for two weeks in 2017 but spent only three weeks on the chart in all, the shortest stay of the group.

Two that came back. Two songs lost the top spot right away and then returned. Cassandra Coleman's ‘Night Air’ debuted at #1 on May 4, 2023, slipped to #2, and went on to spend four weeks at #1 over a 16-week run. Shkodra Elektronike's ‘Zjerm,’ Albania's 2025 Eurovision entry, did the same: it debuted on top on May 15, 2025, dropped to #2, and finished with three weeks at #1.

Repeat offenders. Three acts have debuted at #1 twice. [[Zara Larsson]] did it with ‘Lush Life’ (2016) and ‘Ruin My Life’ (2018), and The Chainsmokers with ‘Closer’ (2016) and ‘High’ (2022). [[Ariana Grande]] did it in back-to-back years: ‘We Can't Be Friends’ opened on top on March 14, 2024 and held #1 for five straight weeks, and ‘Twilight Zone’ followed on April 3, 2025 with four.

2025, the year of the instant #1. No year has more than 2025's six. Besides ‘Twilight Zone’ and ‘Zjerm,’ there were Chappell Roan's ‘The Subway’ in August, [[Demi Lovato]]'s ‘Let You Go’ in October, Chloe Tang and Casandra's ‘Running on Blue’ in December, and Peach PRC's ‘Out Loud’ on Christmas Day. The previous high was four, in 2017. The opposite is true too: 2015, 2019 and 2020 had none at all.

So far 2026 has four: [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ in March, Kim Petras's ‘Need for Speed’ in April, Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me,’ Romania's Eurovision entry, in May, and now Kayla Rae's ‘It Wasn't Nothing,’ her fourth #1 and the first time she has debuted on top. Whether any more arrive this year is up to Will's listening.

headline: Maddie & Tae are the most successful duo in Hot 20 history. Now Maddie Font is starting over on her own
dek: Her first solo EP, ‘Drive Me Around,’ arrives Nov. 6, and its title track is already on the chart. Here's the record she's stepping away from.
body: Last December, [[Maddie & Tae]] told People they would stop working as a duo after 15 years. Taylor Kerr is stepping back to focus on her family, and Maddie Font is carrying on alone, though both said they're leaving the door open to make music together again someday. Font's first solo single, ‘Drive Me Around,’ came out in September, and her debut EP of the same name follows on Nov. 6. It has four songs and is coming out independently.

The duo's numbers. Maddie & Tae put 24 songs on the Hot 20, and 12 of them reached #1. That's more than any other duo or group: [[Lady A]] is next with 10. Only [[Carrie Underwood]] (21) and [[Carly Pearce]] (18) have more #1s, and [[Kenny Chesney]] ties them at 12. Their songs spent 42 weeks at #1 and 413 weeks on the chart in all. The longest stay on top belongs to ‘Die From a Broken Heart,’ with seven weeks in 2018 and 2019.

A slow start, then a streak. Their first four singles all came close without reaching the top. ‘Girl In A Country Song’ peaked at #3 in 2014, then ‘Fly,’ ‘Shut Up and Fish’ and ‘Sierra’ all stopped at #2. ‘After the Storm Blows Through’ finally reached #1 in March 2017 and held it for four weeks. From October 2018 to November 2020, they were on the chart for 108 straight weeks, and that run produced five #1s, from ‘Die From a Broken Heart’ to ‘Water in His Wine Glass.’

The awards shelf. At the Willboard Country Awards, Maddie & Tae won Vocal Duo/Group of the Year seven times: in 2016, then every year from 2019 through 2024. They also won Entertainer of the Year twice, in 2019 and 2020. They're nominated for Vocal Duo/Group again this year, and the winners will be revealed Nov. 18, the night the CMA Awards air.

The last duo hit. Their final Hot 20 appearance was as guests on [[Colbie Caillat]]'s ‘Live Without,’ which reached #3 and left the chart after Feb. 5. That was the last time either of them was on the Hot 20 until this month, an eight-month gap.

Font on her own. ‘Drive Me Around,’ which she wrote with Jonathan Singleton and Brent Anderson, entered at #19 on Oct. 8, held there the next week, and moved to #18 on Oct. 22. The EP also has ‘Make It Up To Me,’ ‘All The Red In California’ and ‘When A Woman Stops Crying.’ That last song is a co-write with Anna Vaus and Taylor Kerr, so the duo's story isn't over on paper either.
Font is starting her solo career with a record that only two acts in Hot 20 history have topped. How the new songs do on the chart is up to Will's listening.

linkText: See the longest runs on the chart
headline: Carly Pearce owns two of the three longest runs in Hot 20 history. The secret is timing, not volume
dek: She stayed on the chart for 116 straight weeks, then 122, almost always with just one song at a time. Here's how the handoffs worked.
body: Only one act has stayed on the Hot 20 longer without a break than [[Carly Pearce]]: [[Ella Langley]], whose run reached 131 straight weeks this month and is still going. Behind her, Pearce holds second and third place, with 122 weeks from March 14, 2024 to July 16, 2026, and 116 weeks from February 25, 2021 to May 11, 2023. [[Kenny Chesney]] (109), [[Maddie & Tae]] (108) and [[Carrie Underwood]] (104) are the only other acts to pass 100. Nobody else has done it twice.

One song at a time. You might expect a streak like that to come from flooding the chart. It didn't. In the 116-week run, Pearce had exactly one song on the Hot 20 in 99 of those weeks, and she never had three at once. The 122-week run was the same story: one song in 81 weeks, never more than two. What kept her there was the timing of each new single.

The first run: five #1s and a #2. ‘Messy’ started it in February 2021 and reached #1. It left the chart on July 1, and ‘29’ arrived the very next week. ‘Never Wanted To Be That Girl,’ her duet with [[Ashley McBryde]], overlapped ‘29’ that fall, and on January 27, 2022, it left the same week ‘Diamondback’ came in. ‘What He Didn't Do’ and ‘All the Whiskey In the World’ each overlapped the song before them by a few weeks. Five of the six songs went to #1, and ‘All the Whiskey’ peaked at #2. When it fell off after May 11, 2023, nothing was waiting behind it, and Pearce spent 43 weeks off the chart.

The second run: six straight #1s. ‘Hummingbird’ ended the break on March 14, 2024 and became the first of six #1s in a row: ‘Hummingbird,’ ‘My Place,’ ‘Truck on Fire,’ ‘Oklahoma,’ ‘If Looks Could Kill’ and ‘No Rain.’ Some handoffs had room to spare, with ‘Truck on Fire’ and ‘Oklahoma’ sharing the chart for nine weeks. Others were as tight as they come. ‘If Looks Could Kill’ left on August 28, 2025 and ‘No Rain’ debuted a week later. ‘No Rain’ left on January 1, 2026 and ‘Dream Come True’ debuted on January 8. Her guest spot on [[Jordan Davis]]'s ‘Mess with Missing You’ added a second song that fall.

How it ended. The run held on through two top-10 singles, ‘Dream Come True’ and ‘If I Don't Leave I'm Gonna Stay’ with [[Riley Green]], each peaking at #10. When ‘If I Don't Leave’ fell off after July 16, 2026, Pearce missed exactly one chart. ‘She Don't’ debuted on July 30, so a single week stands between her and an unbroken run of more than two and a half years. ‘She Don't’ is #9 this week, in its 12th week, and that's a new run of 12 and counting.

The bigger picture. Since her first Hot 20 week on June 29, 2017, Pearce has been on the chart for 424 of its 872 weeks, almost exactly half of them. She has 24 entries and 18 #1s. Long runs on the Hot 20 don't come from stacking songs. They come from having the next one ready the week the last one leaves.

headline: Two #1 acts have new albums out this month. One hasn't charted since 2019; the other just had a #1
dek: Brothers Osborne released ‘Watertown’ on Oct. 23, and Kaitlin Butts follows with ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ on Oct. 30. Here's what each one has done on the Hot 20.
body: October ends with back-to-back Fridays of new country music from two acts who have both topped the Hot 20. [[Brothers Osborne]] released their fifth studio album, ‘Watertown,’ on MCA on Oct. 23. Jay Joyce produced the 11 songs, and the title nods to the Osborne brothers' roots in the blue-collar waterfront town of Deale, Maryland. A week later, on Oct. 30, [[Kaitlin Butts]] releases ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ on Republic Records, previewed by ‘I Wanna Be Bad.’ Their recent Hot 20 runs couldn't be more different.

Brothers Osborne: a slow climb to the top. The duo arrived in June 2015 with ‘Stay A Little Longer,’ which entered at #20 and took 18 weeks to reach #1, on Oct. 22, 2015. It spent one week on top, 20 weeks on the chart in all, and finished #26 for the year. Their next two singles both peaked at #4: ‘21 Summer’ in 2016 and ‘It Ain't My Fault’ in 2017. Two of their seven Hot 20 entries are guest spots, on David Nail's ‘Good At Tonight’ (#8) and Dierks Bentley's ‘Burning Man’ (#7).

Then they went quiet. Their last Hot 20 entry, ‘I Don't Remember Me (Before You),’ peaked at #7 and fell off in May 2019. That's more than seven years without them on the chart. Their debut album, ‘Pawn Shop,’ which carried three of their Hot 20 hits, is still their most-played album on Willboard, with 1,457 plays.

Kaitlin Butts: one of the slowest climbs ever. ‘Marfa Lights’ entered at #20 in January 2022 and needed 26 weeks to reach #1, on July 7, 2022. Only five of the Hot 20's 336 #1s took longer, and ‘Drunk Girl’ is the only other one that also took 26. ‘Marfa Lights’ stayed on the chart for 30 weeks and finished 2022 at #7 on the Year-End list. Her follow-up, ‘She's Using,’ reached #9 that fall.

And a #1 this year. Butts never really left. She's the featured voice on [[Flatland Cavalry]]'s ‘A Life Where We Work Out,’ which entered at #17 on April 2 and reached #1 on July 30, its 18th week. It returned to the top on Aug. 27 for a second week at #1, and it spent 28 weeks on the chart before falling off this month. That gives her two Hot 20 #1s, four years apart, and puts ‘Hello, Honky Tonk’ out while her latest hit is still fresh.

Familiar names in the credits. ‘Watertown’ has two guests with Willboard history. Cody Johnson sings on the opener, ‘Born and Raised Hell’; his only Hot 20 entry, ‘With You I Am,’ reached #7 in 2017. Stephen Wilson Jr. appears on ‘Tough Kid,’ and he's the more recent chart-topper: his duet with Lori McKenna, ‘The Tunnel,’ spent six weeks at #1 from December 2024 into January 2025.
Both of these acts took the long road to #1 the first time. Which songs from these albums reach the chart, if any, is up to Will's listening.

headline: Ten years ago this week: Tim McGraw ran the Hot 20, and a future seven-week #1 entered at #17
dek: A look back at the Hot 20 and Pop 10 of Oct. 27, 2016, and where those songs and artists went next.
body: Ten years ago this week, the Hot 20 of Oct. 27, 2016 belonged to [[Tim McGraw]]. ‘How I'll Always Be’ held #1 for the second of its three weeks on top. McGraw was also all over the rest of the chart. He was featured on Big & Rich's ‘Lovin' Lately’ at #4 and on Florida Georgia Line's ‘May We All’ at #20, so he had three songs in the Hot 20 at once.

The debut that mattered. The quietest move on the chart turned out to be the biggest. [[Little Big Town]]'s ‘Better Man’ entered at #17. Nine weeks later, on Dec. 29, it reached #1, and it stayed there for seven weeks, through Feb. 16, 2017. It finished as the #6 song of 2017 and won Music Video of the Year at the 2017 Willboard Country Awards, where it was also up for Song and Single of the Year.

The rest of the top 5. [[Miranda Lambert]]'s ‘Vice’ sat at #2 and reached #1 two weeks later, on Nov. 10, for two weeks. Lambert is still charting a decade later. Her 34th entry, ‘Two Things Can Be True,’ debuted on this week's Hot 20. [[Chris Stapleton]]'s ‘Parachute’ was at #3 after a week at #1, and Jennifer Nettles's ‘Stupid Girl’ was at #5 after two weeks on top.

Who was just getting started. [[Maren Morris]] was in her first year on the chart, with ‘80s Mercedes’ at #7. It peaked at #3. [[Jon Pardi]] was at #19 with ‘Dirt On My Boots,’ which peaked at #17. He's charted 15 times since 2013, most recently with ‘She Drives Away’ this January. [[Dolly Parton]]'s ‘Pure and Simple’ was at #13 on its way to a #4 peak.
Who wasn't. Florida Georgia Line's ‘May We All’ was the duo's seventh and final Hot 20 entry. It peaked at #11, and they never reached #1.

Over on the Pop 10. [[Meghan Trainor]] and Yo Gotti's ‘Better’ took over at #1 that week and held it for two weeks. It knocked off [[The Weeknd]]'s ‘Starboy,’ down to #3 after two weeks on top. Just below, ‘Starving’ by Hailee Steinfeld, Grey and Zedd sat at #5 after four weeks at #1. It finished as the #6 pop song of 2016. Maroon 5 and Kendrick Lamar's ‘Don't Wanna Know’ was at #2, and Alessia Cara's ‘Scars to Your Beautiful’ was at #8 in its second week.
A different era. In 2016, the Pop 10 was still built by feel. Play tracking didn't arrive until December 2017. The Hot 20 has ranked songs by plays since its first week in 2010.

headline: The CMA Awards and the Hot 20 agree on Ella Langley. They don't agree on much else
dek: With CMA voting closing Oct. 27, we checked every nominee for country's biggest night against a year of Willboard charts.
body: The 60th CMA Awards are set for Nov. 18 in Nashville, with Lainey Wilson hosting. Final-round voting closes on Oct. 27. Ella Langley leads the nominations with nine, followed by Miranda Lambert with seven and Kacey Musgraves with five. The CMAs are voted on by industry members and the Hot 20 is built from Will's own listening, so they were never going to line up exactly. Still, comparing the two says a lot about who's had the year on the radio and who's had it on the Hot 20.

Where they agree: Ella Langley. No act has owned the Hot 20 the way [[Ella Langley]] has. Since July 2025 she has logged 72 chart weeks across six songs, more than anyone else. Four of those songs reached #1, for 13 weeks on top between them: ‘Hungover,’ ‘Choosin' Texas’ (six weeks), ‘Be Her’ (three) and ‘Bottom of Your Boots,’ which is #1 again this week. Both of her Single of the Year nominees, ‘Be Her’ and ‘Choosin' Texas,’ were Hot 20 #1s. Nine nominations sounds like a lot until you look at that run.

The singles race. Only Langley's two Single of the Year nominees reached #1 on the Hot 20. Lainey Wilson's ‘Somewhere Over Laredo’ peaked at #5 and spent 29 weeks on the chart. Taylor Swift's ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ peaked at #6. Cody Johnson's ‘The Fall’ never charted. Musgraves's ‘Dry Spell’ is up for Song and Music Video of the Year after three weeks at #1 this spring, and Carly Pearce and Riley Green's ‘If I Don't Leave I'm Gonna Stay,’ a Musical Event nominee, reached #10.

The women's category is the closest match. Every Female Vocalist nominee has charted recently, and three of the five have had #1s in the past year: Langley and two more. [[Megan Moroney]] has two: ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress,’ whose seven weeks at #1 are the longest run on top this year. [[Kacey Musgraves]] has two as well, ‘Dry Spell’ and ‘Loneliest Girl,’ which held #1 for four weeks. [[Miranda Lambert]] just added her 34th career entry, ‘Two Things Can Be True.’ Lainey Wilson rounds out the field.

Where they don't agree: the men. The male side of the ballot looks very different from the Hot 20. Luke Combs, Chris Stapleton and Cody Johnson are all up for Entertainer of the Year, and none of them has had a Hot 20 entry since 2023. Stapleton's last was ‘White Horse,’ the same song that's up for Music Video of the Year. Johnson's only entry was ‘With You I Am’ in 2017. [[Zach Top]] is the exception. He's up for Male Vocalist and Album of the Year, and he's had two #1s since September 2025, ‘South of Sanity’ and ‘When You See Me.’ [[Stephen Wilson Jr]], up for Male Vocalist, New Artist, Song and Music Video, has one Hot 20 entry, and it was a big one: his duet with Lori McKenna, ‘The Tunnel,’ spent six weeks at #1 from December 2024 into January 2025.

New Artist. Two of the five New Artist nominees are on this week's chart. Emily Ann Roberts's ‘Laundry’ is at #4, her first entry, and Carter Faith's ‘If I Had Never Lost My Mind’ is at #19. Avery Anna and Tucker Wetmore haven't charted.

Who the CMAs left off. Some of the Hot 20's biggest acts this year aren't on the CMA ballot at all. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] has spent 56 weeks on the chart since July 2025, behind only Langley and Moroney and level with Musgraves. That includes the #1 ‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’ and the #2 ‘All In Already.’ [[Danielle Bradbery]]'s ‘Dent’ held #1 for five weeks this winter, and [[Ashley Cooke]]'s ‘Swear Words’ spent three weeks on top. [[The Castellows]] have logged 44 chart weeks without a CMA nomination for Vocal Group.

What it means. The CMAs and the Hot 20 measure different things. One reflects the industry's vote and the other reflects what Will kept coming back to. Where they overlap, though, it's hard to argue: Langley, Moroney and Musgraves have been everywhere on both. The Willboard Country Awards will have their own say. Until then, the CMAs air Nov. 18.

headline: Record of the Year almost always goes to the year's biggest hit. 2026 doesn't have one
dek: Fourteen shows of history, the stat that predicts the winner, and the front-runners, safe bets and dark horses for the 2027 Pop Awards.
body: Song of the Year asks what is on the page. Record of the Year asks about the finished record: how it sounds, how it was built and how hard it landed on the Pop 10. Like the Grammys, the Pop Awards honor the year before the show, so the 2027 show covers songs from roughly mid-November 2025 to mid-November 2026. Nominations aren't final, so this is a read of the field from the chart and from the records themselves. No song can be nominated twice, which rules out the 2026 show's nominees, among them ‘Bite My Tongue’ and ‘Let You Go.’ Agnes's ‘Ego’ sits right on the line, since its week at #1 came on Nov. 13, 2025.

The biggest hit usually wins. In 14 shows, the song that finished its eligibility year at #1 on the Year-End Pop 10 has won Record of the Year 12 times, from ‘Somebody That I Used to Know’ at the 2013 show to ‘Honesty’ at the 2026 show. The two upsets barely count as upsets. At the 2023 show, The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ beat 2022's #1, ‘Unholy,’ and at the 2025 show, Ariana Grande's ‘We Can't Be Friends’ beat 2024's #1, ‘Espresso.’ Both winners were the #2 song of their year. No record ranked lower than that has ever won.

What a winning run looks like. Record of the Year winners have averaged 7.4 weeks at #1, 14 weeks in the top 3 and 21 weeks on the chart. The nominees they beat averaged 3.4, 8 and 13. Weeks at #1 is a weaker predictor than you'd think, though: the winner led or tied its field there only 8 times in 14. Weeks in the top 3 is the stat that matters. The winner led or tied its field there 11 times. The clearest case is the 2018 show, where Demi Lovato's ‘Sorry Not Sorry’ won with a single week at #1 but 11 weeks in the top 3. Voters reward the record that was always there, not the one that peaked hardest.

2026 has no runaway hit. Four songs share the year's longest reign at four weeks each, and no contender is anywhere near the winners' average of 14 weeks in the top 3. The leaders are ‘Obsexxed’ and ‘Brutalist’ with nine each, then ‘Love4Life’ with eight. The lowest total any winner has had is nine, ‘High’ at the 2023 show. That makes this an unusually open race. It also means the Year-End list, which rewards staying power, will matter more than usual.

The December debut. Two of the last three winners had the same quiet advantage. Cassandra Coleman's ‘Habit’ debuted on Dec. 1, 2022, and Nelly Furtado's ‘Honesty’ debuted at #1 on Dec. 19, 2024. Both arrived just after a show's cutoff, so their entire runs counted toward the next year. Three songs have that advantage this time: Kayla Rae's ‘True’ (debuted at #2 on Dec. 4), ‘Running on Blue’ by [[Chloe Tang]] and Casandra (debuted at #1 on Dec. 11) and [[Peach PRC]]'s ‘Out Loud,’ which debuted at #1 on Christmas Day and held for three weeks. None of them had the staying power ‘Honesty’ did, though. ‘Honesty’ spent 24 weeks on the chart, and these ran 10, 6 and 8.

Dark horses get nominated. They don't win. ‘Catch My Breath’ made the 2014 field from #15 on the 2013 Year-End list, ‘Love Me Harder’ the 2016 field from #16, ‘Someone You Loved’ the 2020 field from #13, and ‘Ur So F**king Cool’ the 2021 field from #14. ‘Homura’ made the 2022 field without placing on the 2021 list at all. None of them came close to winning.

The front-runners. [[Chloe Tang]]'s ‘Obsexxed’ spent four weeks at #1 and nine in the top 3 across a 15-week run, the best all-round line in the field. Tang has built her sound on emotionally charged pop with a darker R&B edge, and this May single is where it finally clicked. ‘Running on Blue’ gave her a second #1 this year, which makes her one of only three acts with two, along with Petras and Coleman. [[Willa Ford]]'s ‘Love4Life’ held the top 3 for eight weeks. It's the comeback record of the year: Ford co-produced it with Gustav Afsahi and Jonathan Bluth for her album amanda, and one review singled out the shimmering '80s synth textures around its warm, grateful message. If history holds, the winner is one of these two.

The safe bets for a nomination. [[Kim Petras]]'s ‘Brutalist’ matches ‘Obsexxed’ with nine weeks in the top 3, built on a catchy beat that fades into a quiet, yearning ending. On the stat that matters most, it's a front-runner in all but name. [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis’ debuted at #1 and stayed four weeks; Matthew Koma and Brian Phillips produced it as the opener of an album Rolling Stone called a shimmering synth-pop comeback. Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me’ also debuted at #1 for four weeks. It's a nu-metal Eurovision entry, built from a beat producer Călin Grajdan had on his laptop, that finished third in Vienna. It's the boldest production in the field, though its title drew criticism that could give voters pause. [[Katy Perry]]'s ‘Bandaids’ has the longest run in the window at 16 weeks, a pop-rock ballad on which Perry traded synths for guitars and which Clash called a top-tier heartbreak anthem. And ‘Stateside + Zara Larsson’ is the best-built record of the year: [[Pink Pantheress]] and Oscar Scheller reworked the beat around Larsson's verse, stitching in Adina Howard's ‘Freak Like Me’ and Groove Armada's ‘I See You Baby.’

The dark horses. [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘End of Your Love’ is the one to watch, because its window is still open. It has spent the last three weeks at #1, and every week it adds before the cutoff counts. She co-produced it with Alec Shaw and recorded it with a full band in one room at Sound Emporium in Nashville. With ‘Habit’ at the 2024 show, she's also one of only three acts to win Record and Song of the Year on the same night, alongside Gotye and Maroon 5. Petras's ‘Need for Speed,’ made with Margo XS, Frost Children and nightfeelings, debuted at #1 and held three weeks but lasted only four on the chart, and it may split her support with ‘Brutalist.’ girlsweetvoiced's whispered ‘Cranberry’ had three weeks on top and seven in the top 3, proof that a quiet record can win the chart.

The verdict. On production alone, ‘Stateside’ and ‘Choke Me’ are the most striking records in the race. But Record of the Year has never been decided on sound alone, and in a year without a runaway hit, the top-3 count is the best guide. That points to ‘Obsexxed,’ with ‘Brutalist’ and ‘Love4Life’ close enough to make it a real contest. If there's a third upset in the show's history, look for it near the top of the Year-End list, not from a dark horse.

headline: Megan Moroney is nine for nine in the Hot 20's top 10
dek: ‘Medicine’ reaches #10, and every song she has charted has now made the top 10.
body: [[Megan Moroney]]'s ‘Medicine’ climbs 11-10 on this week's Hot 20. With that, all nine songs she has charted have reached the top 10. It's a perfect record that only a handful of acts have kept going this long.

The run so far. It started at the top. Her first entry, ‘Tennessee Orange,’ debuted in January 2023 and went all the way to #1, and ‘Traitor Joe’ followed it there that summer. ‘I'm Not Pretty’ peaked at #5 and ‘No Caller ID’ at #8. Then came four straight #1s: ‘Mama I Lied,’ ‘Am I Okay,’ ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’ That last one spent seven weeks on top this year, the longest stay at #1 of her career.

Six #1s from nine songs. Two thirds of everything she has released to the chart has gone to #1. ‘Medicine’ is the third charting song from her album Cloud 9, after ‘6 Months Later’ and ‘Wedding Dress.’

The perfect-record club. Moroney joins a short list of acts with at least nine entries that all made the top 10. [[Kip Moore]] leads it by a wide margin: all 21 of his songs have reached the top 10, including ‘Faith in the Wind’ at #8 this week. [[George Strait]], [[Leann Rimes]] and [[Lainey Wilson]] are each 13 for 13, [[Chris Young]] is 11 for 11, and [[The Band Perry]] and [[Morgan Wade]] are 10 for 10.

Awards season. The timing doesn't hurt. Moroney goes into this year's Country Awards with five nominations, including her first for Entertainer of the Year, and ‘Wedding Dress’ is up for both Single and Song of the Year.

headline: Who will win at the 2026 Country Awards? Three experts make their picks
dek: A chart editor, a critic and a fan podcaster call the winners. They don't always agree.
body: The 2026 Country Awards nominations are set, so we asked three very different voices to call the winners. Mitzi Tallyho, Willboard's chart data editor, goes strictly by the past year on the Hot 20: #1s, weeks on top and staying power. Sebastian Crescendo, our senior music critic, cares about craft, meaning the writing, the singing and whether the record says something. Bobbie Jo Rhinestone, host of the fan podcast Windows Down, picks with the heart: the songs that got played the most in the car this year.

Entertainer of the Year. Tallyho picks [[Ella Langley]], and it isn't close on paper. She has four #1s and 13 weeks at #1 over the past year, the most of any nominee, and she's the reigning winner.
