Crescendo goes with [[Megan Moroney]]: “Cloud 9 is the sound of a writer who knows exactly who she is, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Reward the leap.” Rhinestone picks [[Zach Top]]: “Two #1s, the most fun shows in country and a sound that makes 1995 feel brand new.”

Female Vocalist. Tallyho and Rhinestone both pick Langley. Crescendo stays with Moroney, pointing to the restraint of ‘Wedding Dress,’ which a quieter singer would have overplayed. Two votes to one for Langley.

Male Vocalist. Tallyho picks Zach Top, whose ‘South of Sanity’ and ‘When You See Me’ spent seven weeks at #1 between them. Crescendo picks [[David Nail]], whose cover of Bruce Cockburn's ‘Pacing the Cage’ reached #2: “It's the best vocal performance on the ballot, full stop.” Rhinestone picks [[Kip Moore]]: “Twenty-one songs, twenty-one top 10s. He's earned it.”

Vocal Duo/Group. Tallyho picks [[Flatland Cavalry]], the only nominee with a #1 this year (‘A Life Where We Work Out’ with Kaitlin Butts). Crescendo picks [[Maddie & Tae]]: “Their harmonies are still the gold standard, and they're the most decorated act in the show's history for a reason.” Rhinestone picks [[The Castellows]], whose ‘Love Is A Game’ is climbing the chart right now.

New Artist. Tallyho picks [[Mackenzie Carpenter]], who has a #1 (‘Jesus, I'm Jealous’) and two more top 5 hits this year. Crescendo likes Flatland Cavalry's songwriting depth. Rhinestone picks [[Kevin Powers]], whose ‘Move On’ with Shaboozey made it to #1.

Album of the Year. Tallyho picks Langley's Dandelion, which has sent three songs to #1 for a combined 12 weeks. Crescendo picks Moroney's Cloud 9, which reviewers called her most confident work. Rhinestone picks Top's Ain't In It For My Health.

Single of the Year. Tallyho picks ‘Wedding Dress,’ whose seven weeks at #1 are the most of any song on the ballot. Crescendo and Rhinestone both pick ‘Choosin' Texas,’ which Rhinestone calls “the song you sing along to with the windows down,” and Crescendo calls a classic country record in every sense.

Song of the Year. Here Tallyho and Crescendo agree: ‘Wedding Dress.’ For Crescendo, it's the writing of the year: a spare, acoustic song about realizing at the altar that you never got over the one who got away. It turns the fairy tale into something unsettling without a wasted line. Rhinestone goes with ‘Choosin' Texas,’ the story of losing a homesick partner to his Texas hometown and the woman waiting there, told from the long drive back east.

The consensus. Two of our three panelists land on Ella Langley for Female Vocalist and on ‘Wedding Dress’ for Song of the Year. Everything else is up for grabs, which is exactly how an awards night should feel.

headline: Miranda Lambert was there on day one. Her 34th Hot 20 entry proves she never left
dek: ‘Two Things Can Be True’ debuts at #20, putting her one entry behind Carrie Underwood's record.
body: [[Miranda Lambert]]'s ‘Two Things Can Be True’ enters the Hot 20 at #20 this week. It's her 34th entry, second only to [[Carrie Underwood]]'s 35. It extends a chart career that began the very first week the Hot 20 existed.

The first chart. When the Hot 20 began on January 28, 2010, Lambert had three songs on it: ‘White Liar’ at #3, plus ‘Dead Flowers’ and ‘Gunpowder & Lead.’ A few weeks later ‘The House That Built Me’ jumped from #18 to #2 in a single week. More than 16 years on, that's still the biggest one-week climb in the chart's history. It reached #1 three weeks after that.

The records. Lambert has 11 #1s and 28 total weeks at #1. ‘Over You’ ruled for nine weeks in 2012, the longest reign the Hot 20 has seen, a record it now shares with Kenny Chesney and Grace Potter's ‘You and Tequila’ and Kip Moore and Morgan Wade's ‘If I Was Your Lover.’ ‘Tin Man’ added eight more weeks in 2017. Her #1s span 15 years, from ‘The House That Built Me’ in 2010 to ‘Run’ in 2025.

Good company. She's also one of the chart's great collaborators. ‘We Were Us’ with Keith Urban and ‘Santa Fe’ with Parker McCollum both reached #2, and ‘Somethin' Bad’ with Carrie Underwood made #5. She even crossed over to the Pop 10, where ‘Drunk’ with Elle King peaked at #2 in 2021.

The count. At 34 entries, Lambert trails only Underwood. Her 11 #1s tie her with Kip Moore for fifth all-time, behind Underwood (21), Carly Pearce (18), Kenny Chesney (12) and Maddie & Tae (12). Sixteen years after she showed up on the very first chart, her story is still being written.

linkText: See all the 2026 Country Awards nominees
headline: Ella Langley leads the 2026 Country Awards nominations with six
dek: Megan Moroney, Kacey Musgraves and Zach Top follow with five each.
body: Last year's Entertainer of the Year, [[Ella Langley]], leads the 2026 Country Awards with six nominations: Entertainer, Female Vocalist, Album for Dandelion, Single and Song for “Choosin' Texas”, and Music Video for “Be Her”. She won four awards in 2025, including Entertainer and Female Vocalist.

[[Megan Moroney]], [[Kacey Musgraves]] and [[Zach Top]] have five nominations each, and all three join Langley in both Entertainer and Album. Moroney's “Wedding Dress”, which spent seven weeks at #1, is up for Single and Song, and this is her first Entertainer nomination. Musgraves is back in Entertainer for the first time since 2016, with “Loneliest Girl” up for Song. Top won Male Vocalist and New Artist last year and returns in Male Vocalist.

Several acts earn their first nominations. [[Kevin Powers]] leads them with four: Male Vocalist, New Artist, and Single and Musical Event for “Move On” with [[Shaboozey]]. [[Flatland Cavalry]] has three (Duo/Group, New Artist and Musical Event for “A Life Where We Work Out” with Kaitlin Butts), and [[Danielle Bradbery]] picks up two, for Female Vocalist and “Dent” in Single. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]], a New Artist nominee last year, adds three more: Female Vocalist, New Artist and Album for Hey Country Queen.

The veterans are here too. [[Carly Pearce]], already the most nominated act in the show's history, adds two more for 40 in all, including her eighth Entertainer nomination. [[Maddie & Tae]], the show's biggest winners with 16 awards, return in Duo/Group.

headline: Song of the Year rarely goes to the biggest hit. Here's where the best writing of 2026 lives
dek: Fourteen shows say the chart barely matters in this category. A critic's read on the contenders for the 2027 Pop Awards.
body: Record of the Year rewards how a song sounds and how it landed. Song of the Year asks a harder question: what is actually on the page? The 2027 show covers songs from roughly mid-November 2025 to mid-November 2026, and nominations aren't final, so this is a look at the year's Pop 10 through that lens. No song can be nominated twice, so the 2026 show's nominees, among them ‘Bite My Tongue’ and ‘Let You Go,’ are out.

The chart barely matters here. Only three Song of the Year winners finished their year at #1 on the Year-End Pop 10: ‘Somebody That I Used to Know,’ ‘Love Somebody’ and ‘Habit.’ Those are also the only three times Song and Record of the Year have gone to the same song. Since the 2015 show, the two awards have split every year except 2024. The winners have come from all over the Year-End list, as high as #1 and as low as #32, and twice from off the list entirely. Two never reached #1 at all: The Chainsmokers' ‘Everybody Hates Me’ and Kayla Rae's ‘Get Close’ both peaked at #2.

What winners look like. Song of the Year winners have averaged 4.7 weeks at #1 and 8 weeks in the top 3. The nominees they beat averaged 3.0 and 7.0, which is almost the same. The winner led or tied its field in top-3 weeks only three times in 14 shows, and in weeks on the chart only twice. Compare Record of the Year, where the top-3 leader wins most years. The last two winners show the pattern. Cher's ‘DJ Play a Christmas Song’ won at the 2025 show on a three-week holiday run at #1, and Daughtry's ‘Antidote’ won at the 2026 show from #13 after just seven weeks on the chart. A long run gets a song into the conversation. The writing settles it.

‘Brutalist,’ [[Kim Petras]]. The most daring piece of writing of the year. Petras built it from a childhood memory: long drives across Germany with her architect father to get hormone treatment, him critiquing the concrete buildings they passed. The title does double duty, naming the architecture outside the car window and the hard, load-bearing resolve inside it. The chugging, Kraftwerk-style beat keeps the car moving, so the production serves the story instead of decorating it. It's a pop song about something pop rarely touches, told without a speech. On the chart, it spent three weeks at #1 and nine in the top 3.

‘Weather for Tennis,’ [[Hilary Duff]]. The surprise of the year on the page. Duff writes about a relationship where she keeps handing out second chances to someone who keeps breaking promises, then turns the camera on herself, tracing her own avoidance of conflict back to her parents' divorce. That self-implication is what lifts it above a breakup song. The title reads like a forecast for conditions that never quite arrive, which is exactly how the song feels. Written for an album she made with her husband, Matthew Koma, it's the most grown-up writing of her career. It debuted at #1 and stayed there for four weeks.

‘Bandaids,’ [[Katy Perry]]. A song carried by one image, and Perry commits to it: quick fixes on a wound too deep for them. The verses stack smaller pictures on top, flowers sent too late, splinters piling up, the slow sense of flatlining while trying to save something. The central metaphor is familiar, and some lines lean on it a little hard. But the closing turn, admitting she'd choose it all again, gives the song a grace her bigger hits rarely needed. Its 16 weeks make it the longest run in the field.

‘Stateside,’ [[Pink Pantheress]] and Zara Larsson. The best-built song in the field. Its subject is small, the first giddy rush of a crush, and it's stitched together from echoes of Adina Howard's ‘Freak Like Me’ and Groove Armada's ‘I See You Baby.’ Larsson's added verse turns it into a conversation across the Atlantic. As writing it's light, and voters may decide it belongs in Record of the Year. As construction it's close to flawless.

‘Cruel World,’ [[Holly Humberstone]]. A long-distance song about how the world itself seems to warp when the person you love isn't in it. Humberstone has always been strongest at small, specific feelings, and the title track of her second album points that skill at something sunnier without losing it. It peaked at #2 with five weeks in the top 3. That's close to the line of ‘Get Close,’ which won with a #2 peak.

‘Cranberry,’ [[girlsweetvoiced]]. The quietest writing in the race, and on purpose. It's a whispered, shy confession about everyday romance, the kind of song that works by holding back. Its gift is turning shyness itself into the hook.

Two dark horses with history. Kayla Rae's ‘True’ debuted at #2 on Dec. 4 and spent seven weeks in the top 3 without reaching #1, which is the same chart profile as her ‘Get Close,’ the winner at the 2021 show. [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘End of Your Love’ is the title track of an EP about letting go of the life you expected, written and produced with Alec Shaw, and it has spent the last three weeks at #1. Coleman has won this award before, with ‘Habit,’ and she's one of only three acts, with Gotye and Maroon 5, to take Song and Record of the Year on the same night.

The verdict. Plenty of songs had longer runs this year, and history says that won't decide anything. ‘Brutalist’ and ‘Weather for Tennis’ say the most and say it in ways only their writers could. ‘Bandaids’ is close behind on the strength of its ending, and ‘Cruel World’ has exactly the modest, well-placed run this category tends to reward. If Song of the Year is about the song, that's where it should be decided.

headline: Kenny Chesney is back in the top two for the first time since 2019
dek: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at #2, his best placing in almost seven years.
body: “Silver Sands Marina” holds at #2 on the Country Hot 20 this week, its second straight week in the runner-up spot. It is [[Kenny Chesney]]'s first top-two hit since “Tip of My Tongue” spent a week at #1 on November 14, 2019, almost seven years ago.
The song took the long road. It debuted at #18 on July 23 and spent four weeks at #7 before jumping five spots to #2 on October 8.
Chesney never went far in between. “Knowing You” in 2021 and “Just to Say We Did” in 2025 both stopped at #4. “Silver Sands Marina” is his 29th Hot 20 entry, his 24th top 10 and his 19th top 5.

linkText: Every #1 from the Pop 10's first months
headline: The Pop 10 turns 15
dek: How a high school drive became 15 years, 780 charts and 267 #1s.
body: The Pop 10 started the same fall I started driving. Once I had my own car in high school, the radio was on everywhere I went, and it pulled me into pop music in a way nothing had before. I grew to love the genre so much that I gave it a chart of its own. The first Pop 10 arrived on October 27, 2011, and David Guetta and Usher's ‘Without You’ was its first #1.

Before the Pop 10. Pop wasn't new to Willboard. During the transitional era, from January 2010 to October 2011, pop songs competed with country on the Hot 20. Shakira took ‘Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)’ all the way to #1 in 2010, and [[Demi Lovato]] did the same with ‘Skyscraper’ in 2011. [[Lady Gaga]] placed seven songs on the Hot 20, led by ‘Alejandro’ at #3.

The radio years (2011 to 2013). Dev's ‘In The Dark’ finished as the first Year-End #1. Then came the record that still stands: Gotye and Kimbra's ‘Somebody That I Used To Know’ spent 15 weeks at #1 in 2012 and 36 weeks on the chart. Bruno Mars followed with 11 weeks on top for ‘Locked Out of Heaven.’ In December 2013 the chart moved from feel to Spotify playlists.

The mid-2010s. [[Ariana Grande]] and Iggy Azalea's ‘Problem’ ruled 2014 with 10 weeks at #1. In 2015 [[Meghan Trainor]] arrived in a big way, taking the top two spots on the Year-End chart with ‘Like I'm Gonna Lose You’ and ‘Dear Future Husband.’ [[The Chainsmokers]] owned 2016 with nine weeks on top for ‘Don't Let Me Down,’ the start of a run that has made them the chart's second-longest leaders.

Counting the plays (2017 to now). Since December 2017 the Pop 10 has run on real play counts, first from Last.fm and since 2023 from stats.fm. Demi Lovato came full circle with ‘Sorry Not Sorry,’ the 2017 Year-End #1. Sam Smith topped the year twice, with ‘How Do You Sleep’ in 2019 and ‘Unholy’ with Kim Petras in 2022. In 2023 [[Cassandra Coleman]]'s ‘Habit’ came within one week of Gotye's record with 14 weeks at #1. And the chart has gone global: Erika Vikman's ‘Ich Komme’ led for seven weeks in 2025, and the Pop Awards added Foreign Language Song of the Year to honor that year's music.

Milestones. The 100th song to reach #1 was Mariah Carey and YG's ‘I Don't’ on March 2, 2017. Meghan Trainor fittingly brought up #1 number 200 with ‘Made You Look’ on December 1, 2022, and Chloe Tang and Casandra's ‘Running on Blue’ became the 250th last December. Panic! At the Disco's ‘High Hopes’ was the 500th song ever to chart, in November 2018. The 1,000th was [[Hilary Duff]]'s ‘Weather for Tennis,’ which debuted at #1 on March 5 of this year and was still on top a week later for the 750th Pop 10.

By the numbers. Through 780 charts, 267 different songs have reached #1. Meghan Trainor owns the record books with 13 #1s and 42 weeks on top, ahead of The Chainsmokers (34 weeks) and Ariana Grande (32). Here's to the next 15.

linkText: Dolly Parton's full Willboard chart history
headline: Dolly Parton's Willboard legacy: six hits, two charts, and records that still stand
dek: Two months after her death at 80, a look back at her years on the Hot 20 and the Pop 10.
body: [[Dolly Parton]] died on August 25 in Nashville at 80, and on Wednesday night the CMA's two-hour tribute brought country's biggest names together to sing her songs. Her catalog is far older than Willboard, but she found her way onto these charts six times over 13 years, and some of what she did here hasn't been matched.

Where it started. Her first appearance came in the chart's opening weeks. During the transitional era, ‘Jolene’ debuted at #14 on March 18, 2010, and climbed to #8 the next week, more than 35 years after its release. Its four-week run was the first sign that her songs don't belong to any one decade.

‘Home’ (2014). Her signature Willboard moment took patience. ‘Home’ debuted at #17 on July 10, 2014, and spent 14 weeks climbing before it reached #1 on October 9. It held the top spot for two weeks, spent 18 weeks on the chart and finished #14 on the 2014 Year-End chart. She was 68, and 12 years later she is still the oldest woman to top the Hot 20. The song also earned her a Music Video of the Year nomination at the 2015 Country Awards.

‘Pure and Simple’ (2016). The title track of her 2016 album entered at #20 on August 4 and made a slow, steady climb to #4, where it stayed for three weeks. Its 20-week run is her longest on any Willboard chart.

Crossing over (2019). Few country legends have topped the Pop 10, and Parton did it at 73. Galantis' ‘Faith,’ with Mr. Probz, debuted at #6 on November 28, 2019, and reached #1 two weeks later. It led for four straight weeks, carrying her into 2020, and finished #24 on the 2019 Pop Year-End chart. At the time she was the oldest act ever to top the Pop 10. Only Elton John and Cher have since topped it older, and Cher is the only woman to do it.

Still collaborating. She kept showing up alongside younger acts. ‘Happy All the Time’ with Sam Williams, Hank Williams' grandson, reached #12 on the Hot 20 in 2021, and ‘Bets On Us’ with Cheat Codes climbed to #5 on the Pop 10 in January 2023, her last Willboard hit.

By the numbers. Six chart entries, 65 weeks on the charts and six weeks at #1. She is one of only seven acts to send a song to #1 on both the Hot 20 and the Pop 10. Her legacy is much bigger than any chart, but on this one she left a mark that will be hard to touch.

headline: The Pop Awards honor the song, the record and the artist. Should they honor the voice?
dek: What a Best Vocal Performance award would reward, how the Grammys handled the same question, and the songs that would be in the running at the 2027 show.
body: The Pop Awards hand out six trophies: Artist, Record, Song, Album, New Artist and Foreign Language Song. Each one answers a different question. Song of the Year is about the writing. Record of the Year is about the finished production and how hard it landed on the Pop 10. Artist of the Year is about a whole year of work. None of them asks the simplest question a listener has: who actually sang the best? This piece makes the case for a Best Vocal Performance award, lays out how it could work and runs the 2027 field through it. This is a thought experiment, not an announcement, and nothing here changes the 2027 nominations.

What the award would honor. Best Vocal Performance would go to the singer, or singers, on one recording. Not the songwriters, not the producers and not the chart run. It rewards the take you hear: range and control, sure, but also phrasing, restraint, character and the moment where a voice turns a good song into a great one. A whispered vocal can win it as easily as a belted one. That makes it the one award where a modest chart hit can beat a long-running #1 on the merits, and it gives the show a category built for the singers who rarely win Record of the Year because their songs didn't run long enough.

How it mirrors the Grammys. The real-life Grammys have handed out vocal awards since the 1950s, and for decades they were split by gender: Best Female Pop Vocal Performance and Best Male Pop Vocal Performance. At the 54th Grammys in 2012, the Recording Academy folded both, along with Best Pop Instrumental Performance, into a single award, Best Pop Solo Performance. Adele won the first one for ‘Someone Like You,’ and Lola Young won it at the 2026 show for ‘Messy.’ A companion award, Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, covers records with more than one lead act. Both categories are for a single track, and the trophy goes to the performer, not the writers or producers. A Willboard version would follow the modern Grammy model: one award, no gender split, judged on a single recording. The country show already has Male and Female Vocalist of the Year, but those honor an artist's whole year. This would be the pop show's first award for one vocal on one record.

One award or two? The Grammys split solo acts from duos and groups. The Pop 10 history says the Pop Awards might need to as well. Seven of the 14 Record of the Year winners have been duos, groups or collaborations, from Gotye and Kimbra at the 2013 show to The Chainsmokers' ‘High’ at the 2023 show. Collaborations used to be even more common among nominees: 14 of 35 Record nominees from the 2013 to 2019 shows, but only about one in five since. The cleaner option is the Grammys' current setup in a smaller form: one Best Vocal Performance award, open to everyone, with every credited lead singer sharing a win. If duets keep turning up in the field, a separate Duo/Group award could follow later.

The rules. It would use the same window as every other Pop Award, roughly mid-November of one year to mid-November of the next, so the 2027 show covers songs from late 2025 through this fall. It would follow the show's existing rule that no song is nominated twice, which rules out the 2026 field, from ‘Bite My Tongue’ to ‘Honesty.’ The song would need to have charted on the Pop 10 in that window, with a peak cutoff like the top 3 to keep the field focused. One more rule matters: a vocal in any language counts. Foreign Language Song honors the song, but a voice doesn't need translating, and some of this year's strongest vocals weren't sung in English.

The front-runner: Cassandra Coleman, ‘End of Your Love.’ If one record this year was built around a voice, it's this one. It opens with just upright piano and her vocal, and the EP it comes from was recorded with a full band in one room, so what you hear is close to a live take. It reached #1 and held for three weeks. Coleman already swept Record and Song of the Year at the 2024 show with ‘Habit.’ She's also the field's deepest bench, with ‘Maggie’ at #1 and ‘Dying Star’ and ‘Midnight Blue’ in the top 3, though only one of her songs should make the cut.

The duets. Two duet records would make a strong case. ‘Liekinheitin’ by Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen won Finland's UMK this year, and critics singled out Parkkonen's vocal and the chemistry between his voice and Lampenius's violin, which answer each other through the song before its big climax. It spent a week at #1 and six in the top 3. Then there's ‘Bring Your Love,’ the Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter duet that debuted at Coachella and won Best Collaboration at the VMAs. It peaked at #2. Two eras of pop voices on one record is exactly what a vocal award is for.

The safe bets. Holly Humberstone's ‘Cruel World’ is a diaristic song about a long-distance relationship, and she has called it her favorite song she has written. It peaked at #2 with five weeks in the top 3, and quiet, confessional vocals like this are the kind the Grammy category has rewarded. Demi Lovato has two contenders, ‘In My Head’ (#1) and ‘Sorry to Myself’ (#2), and her voice has carried a Record of the Year winner before, ‘Sorry Not Sorry’ at the 2018 show. Kayla Rae's ‘True’ (#2, seven weeks in the top 3) fits here too.

The dark horses. girlsweetvoiced's ‘Cranberry’ is the opposite of a showcase: a whispered vocal that still ran three weeks at #1. A vocal award that only rewards power would miss it, and a good one wouldn't. Alexandra Căpitănescu's ‘Choke Me,’ the nu-metal entry that finished third at Eurovision in Vienna, is the loudest vocal in the field and spent four weeks at #1. Kehlani's ‘Folded’ peaked at #3. Karol G's ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ is a #1 sung in Spanish, and it makes the case for the language rule.

Where the panel lands. Mitzi Tallyho, Willboard's chart data editor, notes that a vocal award would break the pattern of Record of the Year, which the year's biggest hit has won 12 times in 14 shows. ‘Obsexxed’ and ‘Brutalist’ top the 2026 chart race, but neither is a natural pick here. Sebastian Crescendo, Willboard's senior critic, goes with Cassandra Coleman: ‘You build a vocal award for a record like “End of Your Love.” Everything else gets out of the way of the voice.’ Bobbie Jo Rhinestone of the Windows Down podcast takes ‘Liekinheitin’: ‘Nobody I know understands a word of it, and everybody I know has sung along to it in the car.’

The verdict. The Pop Awards already reward the biggest hits, and they should. A Best Vocal Performance award would reward something the chart can't measure. It would follow the Grammys' modern single-award model, stay open to any language and give a trophy to the records people remember for the voice. If it existed at the 2027 show, the smart pick would be ‘End of Your Love,’ the duet to watch would be ‘Liekinheitin,’ and the upset everyone would argue about would be ‘Cranberry.’
